findings.message: When the magic __serialize() and __unserialize() methods are available and the code base does not need to support PHP < 7.4, the implementation of the Serializable interface can be removed. (the class also has __serialize()/__unserialize(), so PHP does not emit the Serializable deprecation)

Since PHP 7.0, functions inspecting arguments, like func_get_args(), no longer report the original value as passed to a parameter, but will instead provide the current value. The parameter "$syntax" was used, and possibly changed (by reference), on line 1030. (PHP 7.0 behaviour: code that runs on PHP 7 or 8 today already gets this behaviour, so the upgrade changes nothing)
